common_conditions.name: Common Cold
recommendations: Take over-the-counter cold medicine if needed
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If symptoms last more than 10 days, fever above 103°F, or difficulty breathing

common_conditions.name: Influenza (Flu)
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If fever persists beyond 3 days, chest pain, confusion, or severe vomiting

common_conditions.name: Migraine
recommendations: Rest in a dark, quiet room
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If headaches are frequent, sudden severe headache, headache with fever and stiff neck

common_conditions.name: Food Poisoning
recommendations: Stay hydrated with ORS or clear fluids
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If symptoms last more than 3 days, blood in stool, high fever, or signs of dehydration

common_conditions.name: Allergic Reaction
recommendations: Use cold compresses for skin reactions
Keep an epinephrine auto-injector if prescribed
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: Immediately if difficulty breathing, throat swelling, dizziness, or rapid heartbeat (anaphylaxis)

common_conditions.name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If blood pressure readings consistently above 140/90, or experiencing severe headache, chest pain

common_conditions.name: Diabetes (Type 2)
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If blood sugar levels are consistently high, symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis, or new symptoms develop

common_conditions.name: Anxiety
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If anxiety interferes with daily life, panic attacks, or thoughts of self-harm

common_conditions.name: Dehydration
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If unable to keep fluids down, very dark urine, rapid heartbeat, or confusion

common_conditions.name: Back Pain
common_conditions.when_to_see_doctor: If pain persists beyond 6 weeks, numbness in legs, bladder/bowel problems, or pain after injury

emergency_signs: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Sudden numbness or weakness (especially one side)
Signs of stroke (FAST: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency)
